title: Cognitive Core stays off the hot order path
statement: The Cognitive Core (slow-thinking planner/scientific engine) must not act as the hot-path trader: no cognitive-core crate or language model is reachable from the reflex cell's order path.
rationale: A slow planner on the order path breaks latency bounds and lets an unbounded model act on orders.

verification.check: Dependency-graph test fails if qip-edge or qip-edge-node can reach qip-ai/qip-reasoning-engine/qip-world-model or a language-model provider; adding such a dependency must turn it red.

title: Cognitive Core decomposes goals
statement: The Cognitive Core can decompose a goal into sub-goals, each a validated goal specification.
rationale: Without decomposition, research and action plans cannot be attributed to the goal they serve.

verification.check: Decomposing a goal yields typed sub-goals and refuses a malformed part; removing validation makes the refusal test fail.

title: Cognitive Core launches research campaigns
statement: The Cognitive Core can launch bounded research campaigns (fetch, verify, backtest, emit results/manifest).
rationale: Research that is not run as a bounded campaign has no manifest and cannot be reproduced.

verification.check: A campaign run produces a manifest and results and deletes its TTL cache; removing the manifest emission fails the test.

title: Cognitive Core calls tools through authorized adapters
statement: The Cognitive Core calls tools only through registered tools with declared authority, and a plan step using an undeclared tool or unheld authority is refused.
rationale: Unregistered tool calls are unattributable external actions.

verification.check: A plan using a lever whose authority the identity lacks is refused; deleting the authority check fails the test.

title: Cognitive Core coordinates specialist agents
statement: The Cognitive Core dispatches work to a governed society of specialist agents and records each run.
rationale: Uncoordinated agents duplicate work and leave no audit of who concluded what.

verification.check: A REASON stage dispatch reaches every specialist and the audit trail records each run; removing an agent from dispatch fails the coverage assertion.

title: Cognitive Core builds causal hypotheses from evidence
statement: The Cognitive Core inspects evidence and forms causal hypotheses whose confidence is computed from that evidence.
rationale: A hypothesis with an asserted confidence cannot be audited.

verification.check: A hypothesis cannot be constructed with a free confidence; drift between stated and evidence-implied confidence is refused.

title: Cognitive Core runs simulations
statement: The Cognitive Core runs simulations (market, scenario, stress) as part of its reasoning loop.
rationale: Untested conclusions reach decisions without any simulated consequence.

verification.check: The SIMULATE stage runs every cycle and reports results; skipping it fails the stage-count test.

title: Cognitive Core requests new data
statement: The Cognitive Core can request new data where it is blind or wrong, producing source-discovery targets.
rationale: A platform that looks only where an operator pointed it never discovers its own blind spots.

verification.check: Forecast-error spikes and knowledge gaps produce ranked discovery targets; removing the forecast-error input empties the targets.

title: Cognitive Core trains models
statement: The Cognitive Core can train models from its learning data as part of the slow lane.
rationale: Without training, discovered patterns never become reusable models.

verification.check: A learning round produces a trained artifact with manifest; removing the training step fails.

title: Cognitive Core challenges its own conclusions
statement: Every hypothesis the Cognitive Core forms is attacked by an adversarial review before it can be acted on.
rationale: A thesis nobody attacked reads as vetted.

verification.check: A hypothesis failing a red-team check is refused; disabling RedTeam lets it through and the test fails.

title: Cognitive Core produces deployable policy/model packages
statement: The Cognitive Core's output is a signed, versioned policy or model package that the warm/reflex lanes can consume.
rationale: Conclusions that are not packaged cannot be deployed or audited by version.

verification.check: The central plane issues a signed policy payload a cell accepts; tampering is refused.

rationale: A scope with no responsible specialist is a blind spot the platform cannot report.

verification.check: The Macro/Geopolitical Brain is constructed in the production organisation and emits findings for its scope; removing it drops its scope from coverage.

title: Communications & Conduct Brain gates external communications
statement: Every authorized external communication passes truthfulness/provenance, identity/disclosure, channel policy, audience/jurisdiction and market-conduct checks before release.
rationale: An ungated publication is a conduct and market-manipulation exposure.

verification.check: A draft failing any single check is blocked; removing one check lets a failing draft through and its independence test fails.

title: Post-publication monitoring of external communications
statement: The Conduct Brain monitors communications after publication.
rationale: A message that becomes misleading after release goes unnoticed.

verification.check: A published message is re-checked after publication and a later violation raises a finding.

title: Block deceptive or manipulative influence patterns
statement: Deceptive or manipulative influence methods have no policy and any plan or communication using one is refused.
rationale: Manipulative influence is unlawful market conduct.

verification.check: A plan using a deceptive method is infeasible; removing the is_deceptive check fails the test.

title: Semantic memory of entities, relationships, definitions, policies
statement: The platform keeps semantic memory: entities, relationships, definitions, policies and stable knowledge, readable point-in-time.
rationale: Without stable knowledge every cycle relearns the world.

verification.check: Knowledge-graph facts are recorded bitemporally and read as-of; lesson promotion requires multiple episodes.

title: Episodic memory of world, belief, action and outcome
statement: The platform keeps episodic memory of what the world looked like, what it believed, what it did, and what followed.
rationale: Without episodes, precedent and attribution have nothing to read.

verification.check: A cycle writes an episode carrying market/world state and belief, and a resolved episode records the outcome gap.

title: Procedural memory of procedures, templates, adapters, playbooks
statement: The platform keeps procedural memory: research procedures, strategy templates, data adapters, playbooks and remediation patterns.
rationale: Procedures that are not memory cannot be reused or improved.

verification.check: A procedure is stored, versioned and retrieved for reuse.

title: Counterfactual memory of rejected and alternate actions
statement: The platform keeps counterfactual memory: what would likely have happened under rejected or alternate actions, never mixed with observed outcomes.
rationale: Learning only from actions taken teaches nothing about vetoes.

verification.check: LEARN prices declined paths and records them apart from observed outcomes.

title: Self-model of weaknesses, blind spots, drift, health, boundaries
statement: The platform maintains a self-model of known weaknesses, blind spots, uncertainty, stale areas, model/data drift, operational health and capability boundaries.
rationale: A platform that weights every component as reliable repeats its errors.

verification.check: Grading a resolved thesis moves the self-model for the producing components and REASON scales evidence by it.

title: Population of specialised world models, not a monolith
statement: The platform maintains a population of world models specialised by domain, geography, horizon, abstraction level and hypothesis, not a single monolithic model.
rationale: One shared model cannot say 'the models disagree'.

verification.check: A population differing on all five axes is registered and every member produces state each cycle.

title: Each world model declares scope, lineage, calibration, cadence, expiry
statement: Each world model has explicit scope, evidence lineage, calibration, update cadence and expiry; a declaration missing any is refused.
rationale: An undeclared model cannot be scored or retired.

verification.check: A declaration missing a field is refused naming it; an expired model is excluded exactly at expiry.

title: Model disagreement preserved as information
statement: Disagreement between world models is preserved and measured, never averaged away; an arbitrated number exists only with its disagreement.
rationale: An average hides that the platform does not know.

verification.check: Arbitration over diverging views keeps every view and the spread; returning a bare merged number fails the type check.

title: Arbitration compares evidence fit, performance, causal coherence, uncertainty
statement: World Model Arbitration compares evidence fit, predictive performance, causal coherence and uncertainty.
rationale: Arbitrating on one dimension rewards a model that is coherent but wrong.

verification.check: Arbitration records all four dimensions and ranks by evidence fit when only that differs.

title: Multiple live branches preserved until reality resolves them
statement: Arbitration can preserve multiple live branches until an outcome resolves them, closing the refuted one with its score.
rationale: Premature merging destroys the alternative that turns out right.

verification.check: Competing branches stay live until resolve(); the refuted branch closes with its Brier score.

verification.check: Advisory cannot be unwrapped except by promote() with a complete case; any order-path crate naming an ambient type fails the scan.

title: NOW Brain estimates latent platform-wide state
statement: A NOW Brain continuously infers the most likely hidden state of markets, economies, companies, supply chains, liquidity, positioning, policy, volatility and system health from incomplete and contradictory observations.
rationale: Collected facts without inference leave the platform with no single estimate of 'now'.

sources.section: §9.6 Global State Estimation Engine - NOW Brain

verification.check: A state estimator updates per observation and returns a state with uncertainty; contradictory inputs widen uncertainty.

title: Every state variable carries confidence, freshness, rate-of-change, diversity, uncertainty
statement: Every NOW state variable carries confidence, freshness, rate-of-change, source diversity and uncertainty.
rationale: A state value without its quality is read as certain.

sources.section: §9.6 Global State Estimation Engine - NOW Brain

verification.check: A state variable missing any of the five fields is refused.

title: State vectors at eight scopes
statement: State vectors exist at global, regional, sector, company, instrument, venue, portfolio and infrastructure scopes.
rationale: A single-scope state cannot answer regional or venue questions.

sources.section: §9.6 Global State Estimation Engine - NOW Brain

verification.check: Each of the eight scopes has a state vector type and estimator.

title: Competing state estimators contribute estimates
statement: Bayesian/state-space filters, neural state-space models, graph models, causal models and symbolic constraints can contribute competing state estimates.
rationale: A single estimator's failure mode becomes the platform's.

sources.section: §9.6 Global State Estimation Engine - NOW Brain

verification.check: Two estimators for one variable both contribute and their disagreement is recorded.

title: High-surprise state change wakes specialists
statement: A state change with high surprise automatically wakes relevant forecast, adversarial, sensing and risk specialists.
rationale: A material surprise that wakes no one is a missed warning.

sources.section: §9.6 Global State Estimation Engine - NOW Brain

verification.check: A high-surprise change produces AttentionEvents to the four pathways.

title: NOW Brain persists compact state and belief deltas only
statement: The NOW Brain persists compact state and belief deltas, not raw world payloads.
rationale: Copying raw world payloads is unbounded retention and a licensing exposure.

sources.section: §9.6 Global State Estimation Engine - NOW Brain

verification.check: Persisted NOW records contain only deltas; a raw payload field fails the schema.

title: External evidence re-fetchable by manifest

rationale: Evidence that cannot be re-fetched cannot be re-verified.

sources.section: §9.6 Global State Estimation Engine - NOW Brain

verification.check: Each NOW delta cites a manifest entry resolvable to a source reference.

title: Forecasts organised as a lattice of linked horizons

rationale: A single-horizon forecast cannot be calibrated per horizon.

verification.check: Each lattice horizon has registered models and a calibration series; per-horizon Brier is emitted.

title: Horizons constrain one another
statement: Higher-level state and lower-level microstructure forecasts continuously constrain one another across the lattice.
rationale: Inconsistent horizons produce contradictory positions.

verification.check: A forecast inconsistent with its adjacent horizon is flagged or reconciled.

rationale: A model promoted to the wrong lane breaks latency or authority bounds.

verification.check: A Microseconds-ms model targeting any lane other than Local Reflex only is refused at admission.

statement: Forecasters earn or lose influence from calibration, incremental information value, regime-specific accuracy, cost and latency.
rationale: Influence by authority or size rewards confident, wrong models.

verification.check: An ensemble weight moves with each of the five factors; a model with poor calibration loses weight.

title: Forecaster disagreement preserved as research signal
statement: Disagreement among forecasters is preserved and becomes a research signal.
rationale: Discarded disagreement is lost information about what the platform does not know.

verification.check: Material disagreement raises a research task citing the record.

title: Model Tournament scores by regime
statement: A Model Tournament continuously scores Brier, log loss, calibration, tail accuracy, economic usefulness and robustness by regime.
rationale: A single global score credits a model for conditions it was never tested in.

verification.check: Tournament output has all six metrics per model per regime; dropping one fails the schema test.

title: Forecast Market assigns synthetic reputation capital
statement: A Forecast Market gives models synthetic reputation/capital so aggregate probabilities reflect measured historical skill, not model size.
rationale: Aggregation by authority overweights large, uncalibrated models.

verification.check: Aggregate probability weights equal reputation shares derived from scored history.

title: Ephemeral specialists spawned and retired
statement: Ephemeral specialists may be spawned for a company, election, supply shock, weather system, protocol, product or event and retired after relevance decays.
rationale: Permanent specialists for transient questions waste compute and go stale.

verification.check: A spawned specialist carries an expiry and is excluded once expired.

title: Meta-models predict forecaster failure and reweight
statement: Meta-models predict which forecasters are likely to fail under the current regime and dynamically adjust ensemble weights.
rationale: Static weights keep trusting a model through the regime it fails in.

verification.check: Ensemble weights change on a regime change predicted to break a forecaster.

title: Continuously evolving tree of plausible futures
statement: The platform maintains a continuously evolving tree of plausible futures.
rationale: Without branches the platform plans for one future.

sources.section: §9.9 Future-State Tree, Synthetic Worlds & Digital Twins

verification.check: A future tree exists in the cycle and is updated as observations arrive.

title: Synthetic-world generators vary causal assumptions
statement: Synthetic-world generators vary causal assumptions, participant behavior, policy, liquidity, weather, supply constraints, defaults, market structure and Algorik actions.
rationale: Simulating only history cannot test unseen worlds.

sources.section: §9.9 Future-State Tree, Synthetic Worlds & Digital Twins

verification.check: A generator produces worlds differing along the named dimensions.

title: Digital twins use compact learned state, not copied world data
statement: Digital twins model economically important entities using compact learned state rather than copied world data.
rationale: Copied world data is unbounded and licence-exposed.

sources.section: §9.9 Future-State Tree, Synthetic Worlds & Digital Twins

verification.check: Twin state contains no raw source payload.

title: Branches carry probability, assumptions, evidence, propagation, impact, hedges
statement: Each future branch carries probability, causal assumptions, unresolved evidence, expected market propagation, portfolio impact and hedge requirements.
rationale: A branch without impact and hedge needs cannot drive a decision.

sources.section: §9.9 Future-State Tree, Synthetic Worlds & Digital Twins

verification.check: A branch missing any of the six fields is refused.

title: Reality prunes, reweights or splits branches
statement: Arriving observations continuously prune, reweight or split future branches.
rationale: A tree that never updates is a static scenario set.

sources.section: §9.9 Future-State Tree, Synthetic Worlds & Digital Twins

verification.check: An observation consistent with one branch reweights it; a contradicting one prunes.

title: Exchange/venue twins simulate queueing, latency, fills, slippage, impact, responses
statement: Exchange/venue twins simulate queueing, latency, fills, slippage, market impact and participant responses.
rationale: A generous simulator makes every strategy look better than it is.

sources.section: §9.9 Future-State Tree, Synthetic Worlds & Digital Twins

verification.check: SimBook sweep never fills beyond published depth; impact and latency applied.

title: Macro/company/supply-chain twins explore second/third-order propagation
statement: Macro, company and supply-chain twins explore second- and third-order propagation paths before they are obvious in prices.
rationale: First-order exposure misses the dependency that hits the book.

sources.section: §9.9 Future-State Tree, Synthetic Worlds & Digital Twins

verification.check: Propagation names instruments two hops from a driver the book depends on.

title: Rare-event factories synthesize unprecedented combinations
statement: Rare-event factories deliberately synthesize unprecedented combinations so risk and hedge systems learn outside historical experience.
rationale: Risk trained only on history fails on the first novel crisis.

sources.section: §9.9 Future-State Tree, Synthetic Worlds & Digital Twins

verification.check: Generated scenarios include combinations absent from the historical library.

title: Expected value of information computed for major uncertain decisions
statement: Every major uncertain decision can calculate the expected value of additional information and launch the cheapest lawful observation most likely to discriminate between competing worlds.
rationale: Deciding without asking what to observe next wastes cheap disambiguation.

verification.check: A decision with high uncertainty produces an InfoRequest choosing the cheapest discriminating source.

title: Information requests trigger many acquisition kinds
statement: Information requests may trigger a new source query, alternative provider, microstructure probe, simulation, specialist agent, public filing fetch or additional measurement.
rationale: One acquisition kind leaves cheaper disambiguators unused.

verification.check: Each request kind dispatches to its handler.

title: Curiosity Engine ranks by significance x uncertainty reduction x urgency x cost
statement: The Curiosity Engine ranks research by economic significance x uncertainty reduction x urgency x acquisition cost.
rationale: A ranking that ignores any factor buys expensive, irrelevant or late information.

verification.check: Ranking is monotone in each factor as the formula states; zeroing any multiplicative factor zeroes the score.

title: Evidence acquisition stops at marginal value or deadline
statement: Evidence acquisition stops when marginal information value falls below compute/data cost or the decision deadline passes.
rationale: Unbounded acquisition burns cost after the decision is made.

verification.check: should_halt is true at the deadline and when net value is below minimum.

title: Important forecasts attacked by eight named critic kinds
statement: Every important forecast is attacked by independent bull, bear, structural-break, manipulation, tail-risk, model-risk, data-poisoning and missing-variable critics that attempt to falsify the leading explanation.
rationale: A critic set missing a kind leaves that failure unchallenged.

verification.check: Each of the eight critics runs on a hypothesis and can refuse it.

title: Authority only by surviving challenge and staying calibrated
statement: A conclusion gains authority only by surviving independent challenge and maintaining calibration over time.
rationale: Authority by assertion lets an unchallenged or miscalibrated source drive capital.

verification.check: A hypothesis refused by review cannot reach DECIDE; an origin with a poor record is down-weighted.

title: Meta-Intelligence allocates compute by expected uncertainty reduction or value
statement: The Meta-Intelligence Brain decides which questions, models, agents, simulations and solvers receive another unit of CPU/GPU/TPU/QPU capacity based on expected uncertainty reduction or expected economic value.
rationale: Compute allocated by habit scales cost, not intelligence.

verification.check: Allocation records rationale and the expected value it was granted on.

title: Model reputation by domain, horizon and regime
statement: The Meta-Intelligence Brain maintains model reputation by domain, horizon and regime.
rationale: A global reputation credits models for regimes they were never tested in.

verification.check: Reputation for an unseen regime cell reads as uninformed, not the global average.

title: Marginal value of extra simulation, agent, call, source or QPU experiment measured
statement: The platform measures the marginal value of an additional simulation, agent, model call, data source or QPU experiment.
rationale: Without marginal value, spend cannot be stopped where it stops paying.

verification.check: A marginal-value figure is recorded per added unit.

title: Create specialist populations where residual error is economically meaningful
statement: The Meta-Intelligence Brain creates new specialist populations when residual error remains economically meaningful.
rationale: Persistent residual error with no new specialist is a known blind spot left open.

verification.check: Residual above threshold proposes a new specialist.

title: Kill redundant or persistently unproductive work
statement: The Meta-Intelligence Brain kills redundant or persistently unproductive work so scaling follows value, not agent count.
rationale: Unbounded agent count is uncontrolled cost.

verification.check: Work unproductive for N windows is retired.

title: Cognitive Compiler distils verified capability into bounded packages
statement: Validated discoveries pass through symbolic formalisation and specialist training, and the Cognitive Compiler distils verified capability into bounded warm/reflex packages.
rationale: Slow-lane discoveries otherwise never become fast, deterministic intelligence.

verification.check: A verified discovery yields a compiled bounded package with stated cost that the cell can load.

title: No frontier model called from the order path
statement: Fast intelligence derived in the slow lane runs without calling a frontier model from the order path.
rationale: A model call on the order path is unbounded latency and unbounded authority.

verification.check: Architecture test fails if an edge cell can reach a language model.

title: Typed Forecast contract for every material prediction
statement: Every material prediction uses a typed Forecast contract containing outcome distribution, horizon, target variable, epistemic uncertainty, aleatoric uncertainty, tail mass, model disagreement, regime confidence, expected impact, evidence lineage and expiration.
rationale: A prediction without decomposed uncertainty and expiry cannot be calibrated or retired.

verification.check: A Forecast missing any field is refused on decode; every material prediction site constructs one.

title: Calibration is a production SLO
statement: Calibration is a production SLO with an objective and alerting, not only a research metric.
rationale: A metric nobody alerts on lets the platform drift into overconfidence unnoticed.

verification.check: An SLO/alert policy on the calibration series exists and plans; removing it fails the infrastructure acceptance suite.
